title: Relative error tends to zero
statement: For each natural number $w$, define the critical size as the greatest $s\le 2^{w+2}$ satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le 1/2$, and define the critical dimension as $w$ times that size. Let the coordinate influence be $2^{-(w-1)}(1-2^{-w})^{s-1}$, with $s$ the critical size, and let the relative error be the coordinate influence times the critical dimension, divided by the logarithm of the critical dimension, minus $1$. As $w\to\infty$, this relative error is $o(1)$.
hypotheses_covered: The critical size is the greatest qualifying $s\le 2^{w+2}$
The critical dimension is $w$ times the critical size
The relative error is the influence times the dimension divided by its logarithm, minus $1$
The relative error is little-o of the constant function $1$ as $w\to\infty$
